lessons.lesson: Extreme fear (Fear & Greed below 25) is followed by BTC/ETH being higher a week later more often than not: crowds sell in panic, prices rebound.
lessons.source: Common contrarian belief; untested here. Evidence on sentiment indices is mixed.

lessons.lesson: Extreme greed (Fear & Greed above 75) is followed by BTC/ETH being lower a week later more often than not: FOMO buying runs out.

lessons.lesson: High perpetual funding (crowded leveraged longs, above 0.03% per 8 hours on average) is followed by a lower price a day later more often than not.
lessons.source: Crypto derivatives research suggests extreme funding marks crowded positioning; the effect size is uncertain.

lessons.lesson: Below its 50-day average, a coin is lower a week later more often than not (trends persist). This is the idea behind the desk's trend rule.
lessons.source: Time-series momentum (Moskowitz, Ooi and Pedersen 2012; Liu and Tsyvinski 2021 for crypto); our 2020-26 backtest (docs/crypto-desk.md).

lessons.lesson: My calls are worse than the no-skill baseline when volatility is high: overconfidence. Under this tag, stay close to 50% and the baseline range.
lessons.source: Overconfidence (Barber and Odean 2000, 2001); untested for this analyst.

lessons.lesson: After a move of more than 5% in 24 hours, my calls chase the move (recency bias) and score worse than the baseline.
lessons.source: Recency and attention effects (Barber and Odean 2008); untested for this analyst.
